sources.title: GPT-5 Pro — model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact gpt-5-pro alias points to gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06; 400,000 context, text/image input, text output, file uploads, function calling and high-only reasoning. Responses is the supported interactive endpoint. No code interpreter. Page marks the model deprecated. Reopened October 27, 2026 through the documentation connector and read the complete freshly fetched model Markdown; no total or active parameter count is listed.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5
sources.evidence: August 7, 2025 announcement explicitly releases GPT-5 Pro to ChatGPT Pro subscribers and describes it as the GPT-5 variant using parallel test-time compute. Freshly reopened October 27, 2026; its Pro section provides no numerical total or active parameter specification.

sources.title: API changelog — October 6, 2025
sources.evidence: The October 6, 2025 API entry announces GPT-5 Pro at DevDay as a version of GPT-5 using more inference compute. This is later than the original ChatGPT release.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026 (60-page original PDF; complete extracted text searched). Sections 1 and 3 explicitly define gpt-5-thinking-pro as gpt-5-thinking using parallel test-time compute. Model data/training and comparison sections provide no nominal total or active count. The text has no model-parameter, billion or trillion count; its activated occurrence concerns human review. This is scoped negative evidence from the checked source, not proof that no disclosure exists anywhere.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: The Responses API accepts file inputs; for models with vision, PDF processing supplies both extracted text and page images. This applies to the exact model's documented image and file-upload support.

sources.title: Deprecations — GPT-5 and o3 models
sources.evidence: June 11, 2026 notice gives December 11, 2026 as the API shutdown date for gpt-5-pro and gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06; this is future-dated at review time.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement effective January 1, 2026 grants limited service access and reserves service IP rights under sections 2.2 and 9.1. Supports descriptive proprietary hosted-service classification, not a weight license.

sources.title: All models
sources.evidence: Current catalog separately lists gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b as Apache-2.0 open-weight models and GPT-5 Pro among hosted models, corroborating the closed-weight classification.

sources.title: Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026 (89-page original PDF; complete extracted text searched). The November 20, 2025 report examines named GPT-5 Pro scientific case studies. Its model-use sections provide no total or active model-weight count. Parameter and activated matches concern mathematical/physical problems or immune cells, not network sizes; no nominal model count was found.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27, 2026 using the complete freshly fetched original PDF text and a new direct HTTP-200 PDF fetch after the web renderer failed. November 12, 2025 comparison tables concern GPT-5 Thinking/Instant and GPT-5.1 successors and report safety metrics, not total or activated parameters. No numeric count for GPT-5 Thinking is available to transfer through its explicit Pro relationship.

sources.title: GPT-5 — model documentation
sources.evidence: The underlying GPT-5 reasoning model explicitly supports prompt caching and cached-input pricing. Used only with the system card's explicit Pro-as-GPT-5-thinking relationship for broad architecture inheritance, not to assert Pro endpoint caching support. Read the complete freshly fetched GPT-5 model Markdown again October 27, 2026: it provides no nominal total or active count for the explicitly named base of Pro.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: February 18, 2026 technical guide, archived and explicitly scoped to models before GPT-5.6, explains OpenAI prompt caching through transformer attention-layer key/value projections and tensors. Supplies the mechanism for a qualified broad Transformer inference from GPT-5 caching support.

sources.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
sources.evidence: April 23, 2026 original research report, reopened October 27; complete 31-page extracted text searched and Results, Methods and Supplementary Table 2 inspected. Exact GPT-5 Pro appears alongside later Pro models. The table reports pass rates, token accounting and replicate counts, with Pro token totals omitted; it has no parameter-count column. Methods describe a separate Pro harness, not a numerical model size. No total or active model-weight count was found.

sources.title: LongCat-Flash-Thinking Technical Report — Table 2
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened original report October 27, 2026 and cross-checked the team's GitHub README Evaluation Results table. Table 2 explicitly separates Total Params and Activated Params but marks both GPT-5-Thinking entries with dashes. The comparison model is the named reasoning model underlying Pro, not an independently specified Pro checkpoint. This later original model-team table supplies neither number and cannot support a numerical lineage inference.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Fresh search lead reopened in the July 5, 2026 original revision; abstract, Section 6.3/Table 2 and Appendix E/Table 15 checked. Table 2 gives GPT-5 Pro a calibrated effective-knowledge-capacity estimate, not a developer specification or measured production parameter count. Table 15 leaves actual Params and Arch as dashes for gpt-5-pro. Excluded from both audited counts; its black-box lineage suggestions are also unnecessary given OpenAI's explicit model relationship.

name.note: Exact official public name and API alias; the system card calls the inference setting gpt-5-thinking-pro.

developer.note: Original developer and official model publisher.

family.note: Normalized GPT-5 family. Pro is an inference variant of GPT-5 thinking, not a separate GPT-Pro model lineage.

release_date.note: Earliest public release of the named GPT-5 Pro model was in ChatGPT on August 7, 2025. The gpt-5-pro API rollout and dated snapshot followed October 6, 2025. This undated named-model record uses earliest public release; API limits below describe the October snapshot, not the original ChatGPT deployment.

open_weights.note: Hosted API/ChatGPT model with no released weight artifact; OpenAI separately identifies its open-weight gpt-oss models. Classification applies to GPT-5 Pro, not the GPT brand as a whole.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted service under OpenAI terms, not an SPDX identifier or open-weight license. Current terms are not claimed to be identical to the original 2025 terms.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit found no supported nominal total in the exact GPT-5 Pro/GPT-5 specs, original launch/system card, later science and GPT-5.1 reports, or GeneBench. OpenAI explicitly identifies Pro as GPT-5 Thinking with parallel test-time compute, so a published base count would support nominal lineage; no such count was found. Meituan's later original Table 2 leaves GPT-5-Thinking Total Params blank. Targeted exact-Pro total/active and later-report searches surfaced IKP black-box estimates, which are not specifications. Null reflects absent supported nominal evidence, not a requirement for a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately from total. No nominal activated-parameter count was found in the complete searched source texts or inspected model/comparison sections. Meituan Table 2 explicitly leaves GPT-5-Thinking Activated Params blank; OpenAI's later GeneBench exact-Pro table reports performance and run statistics without a parameter column. Parallel test-time compute and Pro-harness execution do not establish active weight counts or MoE topology. No total-to-active equality, unrelated sibling transfer or black-box estimate is used.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source inference: OpenAI explicitly defines Pro as GPT-5-thinking with parallel test-time compute; its GPT-5 API model supports prompt caching, and the pre-GPT-5.6 caching guide describes Transformer attention KV tensors. Supports only broad Transformer-based inheritance, not a direct Pro block-layout disclosure, exclusive use of Transformer layers, or dense/MoE topology. The Pro endpoint itself does not list cached-input pricing.

context_window.note: Exact gpt-5-pro API documentation gives 400,000 tokens for default gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06. Do not substitute max output tokens or ChatGPT plan context limits; endpoint operation was not tested.

modalities.note: Native modalities are text/image input and text output. PDF is additionally recorded as the supported API file-input format: the exact model lists image input, file uploads and Responses support; the file guide specifies extracted text plus page images for vision models. Tool-generated images are not native model image output. No native audio/video claim.

reasoning.note: Exact API model supports reasoning tokens and only reasoning.effort high; Pro increases inference compute. This is distinct from ChatGPT's router and its non-reasoning Instant model.

tool_call.note: Exact model lists function calling and Responses tools including web/file search and MCP. Code interpreter is explicitly unsupported; tool calling does not imply every tool is available.

patch.notes: GPT-5 Pro first became publicly available in ChatGPT on 2025-08-07; the gpt-5-pro API alias and gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06 snapshot launched on 2025-10-06. The 400,000-token context and API capabilities refer to that documented API snapshot, not original ChatGPT plan limits. The system card defines Pro as GPT-5-thinking with parallel test-time compute. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked primary sources; no published base count supports a numerical lineage inference, and extra inference compute does not establish a larger checkpoint or MoE topology. Broad Transformer-based architecture is a qualified inference from that explicit model relationship, GPT-5 prompt-caching support, and OpenAI's pre-GPT-5.6 attention-KV caching explanation; Pro endpoint caching support is not asserted. PDF denotes API preprocessing into text and page images. Only high reasoning effort is supported; code interpreter is unsupported. The alias and snapshot were deprecated on 2026-06-11 with announced API shutdown on 2026-12-11, still in the future at review time. No live inference request was made.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts as explicit nulls. Reopened exact GPT-5 Pro/GPT-5 specifications, launch and original system card; searched complete original paper texts and inspected later science, GPT-5.1, GeneBench and Meituan comparisons. Meituan explicitly leaves total/activated counts blank for the named GPT-5-Thinking base; GeneBench includes exact Pro without a parameter column. No supported nominal base count enables lineage inference. IKP black-box estimates were excluded. Preserved the other 12 field assessments and their existing corrections.
